title: Prompt-reference failures are loud and coded — and a stored `model` is inert on the media path
summary: Two things agents get wrong about saved prompts, both because the first shipped documentation described pre-fix behaviour. (1) A reference that cannot resolve does NOT silently degrade into a normal call. Every failure raises with a code: prompt_reference_needs_project (400) when `prompt.<handle>` arrives without a project_id, prompt_not_found (404) for an unknown handle or id, and prompt_reference_ambiguous (409) when two names slugify onto one handle — in which case the resolver names both candidates' ids rather than picking one. An agent that treats a failed reference as 'it'll just generate without it' will see a 4xx and no output. (2) `prompt.<handle>` resolves by slug OR exact name, not by exact name alone: one query does `name = $3 OR slug(name) = $4`, which is why both the dashboard-printed slug and the raw name address the same prompt, and why colliding slugs are still individually addressable by their exact names. (3) The stored `model` in a bundle is unreachable on the MEDIA path: generate-media declares `model` as required with min_length=1, so the 'fill in only if the caller set none' branch can never fire — omitting it is a 422 and an empty string is a 422. The stored model does apply on the chat path, where model is optional. The stored settings, system_prompt and reference_media_ids apply on both.
references: app/services/gate/prompt_service.py:73 — _SLUG_SQL = btrim(regexp_replace(lower(btrim({col})), '[^a-z0-9]+', '_', 'g'), '_'); :428 — the resolve query, `AND (name = $3 OR <slug> = $4)`, one query so >1 row IS the collision signal rather than a silent LIMIT 1
